description:
Split out of GH#18 (https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/kopitiam/issues/18), where
the reporter noted it but deliberately did not file it separately.

On an UNMODIFIED tree, `cargo test --release -p kopi-beans` gave a release-mode
failure count that varied between 10, 11 and 12 across repeated runs. The
`daemon::runtime::*` tests (WAL, failpoint, HLC) are the suspects.

Why it matters: non-deterministic failures mean "did my change break anything?"
cannot be answered without running a baseline on a clean worktree first — every
single time. That is the exact cost this tracker exists to remove.

Two permanent (deterministic) failures in that count are bd-ef2's tombstone
tests; this bead owns the REST — the ones that move.

First step is measurement, not a fix: run the suite N times on a clean tree,
record which test names appear in the failing set and how often, then decide
per-test whether it is a real race (HLC ordering, WAL fsync timing) or a test
harness timing assumption that got tighter under release optimisation.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
2026-08-13, from the bd-ef2 agent's baseline runs — SHARPENS this bead considerably:

`daemon::runtime::core::tests::restores_hlc_state_for_non_daemon_actor` is NOT flaky.
It failed 3/3 on re-run in release. Deterministically red:

    thread panicked at crates/kopi-beans/src/daemon/runtime/core/mod.rs:3527:9:
    assertion failed: restored > persisted

Pure HLC/WAL path (`wal_index.reader().load_hlc()`, `WriteStamp` comparison), zero
tombstone involvement, so definitely not collateral from the bd-ef2 assert_eq change.

So the ~10-12 figure from GH#18 is really TWO populations, and they need splitting:
  (a) deterministic reds like this one — a real bug, reproducible, fix it properly;
  (b) genuinely varying ones — the actual flakes.
Do the N-run tally first and label each failing test (a) or (b) before touching code.
Chasing a deterministic bug as if it were a race wastes the whole session.

Also useful: `cargo test --release -p kopi-beans --lib core:: -- --skip daemon::` is
clean at 364 passed / 0 failed, so `core::` is a trustworthy signal today. The rot is
confined to `daemon::runtime`.

title: kopi-beans: daemon::runtime WAL/failpoint/HLC tests are flaky in release (10-12 failures, varies per run)
